                                <div class="heading_H"><h1>Differences between PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments 'have eased'</h1></div>
                                    <div class="except" style="margin-bottom: 12px;">
                        <h2>Bilawal’s inclusion in JCP significant in the context of PPP’s reported demand for greater say in judicial appointments</h2>
                    </div>
                                <div class="time-section"  >
                                            <div class="source">
                                                            <span class="by_author">By</span>



        <div class="author_title_img" style="color:#000">
                            <a href='https://www.geo.tv/writer/ansar-abbasi'>Ansar Abbasi</a>

                        </div>
                                <span class="author_seperator"> | </span>
                            <p class="post-date-time">
                              Published October 10, 2026                            </p>
                        </div>
                                        
                </div>
            </div>
            <div class="left">
                <div class="story-area">
                    <div class="content-area">
                        <div class="medium-insert-images ui-sortable"><figure contenteditable="false">
    <img src="https://www.geo.tv/assets/uploads/updates/2026-10-10/685881_6775539_updates.jpg" alt="This representational image shows a gavel and scales of justice. — Reuters/File" width="700" height="400" class="">

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">This representational image shows a gavel and scales of justice. — Reuters/File</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b>Induction comes amid differences between two coalition partners.</b></li><li><b>Sources say differences between PPP and PML-N have eased.</b></li><li><b>Next meeting for JCP is scheduled this month on October 13.<br></b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: The induction of Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) Senator Rana Sanaullah into the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) comes amid recent differences between the two coalition partners over appointments to the superior judiciary, with sources suggesting that a fresh understanding could lead to reconsideration of PPP-backed candidates.</p><p>The two leaders were formally appointed members of the commission following the resignations of PPP Senator Farooq H Naek and PML-N member Sheikh Aftab Ahmad. Bilawal will represent the treasury benches in the National Assembly, while Rana Sanaullah will represent the Senate.</p><style>

	<ins class="adsbygoogle"
	     style="display:inline-block;width:300px;height:250px"
	     data-ad-client="ca-pub-7369466212570555"

	<script>
	     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
	</script>
	</div><p>The appointments follow months of reported dissatisfaction within the PPP over its inability to secure the commission’s approval for several candidates it had supported for judicial positions.</p><p>According to media reports, Senator Farooq H Naek had proposed 33 candidates for appointments to the high courts: 16 for the Sindh High Court, 10 for the Lahore High Court, five for the Balochistan High Court and two for the Islamabad High Court. These reports said the PPP failed to secure approval for its preferred candidates in the relevant deliberations.</p><p>Sources familiar with the latest political discussions now suggest that differences between the PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments have eased. They believe the evolving understanding between the coalition partners could provide an opportunity for some PPP-backed candidates to be reconsidered in future rounds of appointments.</p><p>However, the extent of any such understanding, and whether it includes agreement on specific candidates, remains unclear. There is also no public confirmation of such an understanding by the two parties.</p><p>Bilawal’s inclusion in the commission is particularly significant in the context of the PPP’s reported demand for a greater say in judicial appointments. The party had previously expressed dissatisfaction after its preferred candidates failed to obtain the necessary support, while its senior legal representative, Farooq H Naek, had proposed candidates for several high courts. Apparently for the same reason, the Presidency had recently delayed approval of many appointments. The commission’s composition has become an important factor in the debate over judicial appointments following constitutional changes that expanded parliamentary representation in the process. Its decisions, however, continue to depend on the commission’s voting procedure.</p><p>The JCP’s next meeting is scheduled for October 13, 2026, with the extension of the term of the Sindh High Court’s constitutional benches on the reported agenda.</p><p></p>    <p class="canonical-url">

      </i>
    </p>

headline: Differences between PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments 'have eased'
subheadline: Bilawal’s inclusion in JCP significant in the context of PPP’s reported demand for greater say in judicial appointments
author: Ansar Abbasi
article_text:
Induction comes amid differences between two coalition partners.
Sources say differences between PPP and PML-N have eased.
Next meeting for JCP is scheduled this month on October 13.

ISLAMABAD: The induction of Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) Senator Rana Sanaullah into the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) comes amid recent differences between the two coalition partners over appointments to the superior judiciary, with sources suggesting that a fresh understanding could lead to reconsideration of PPP-backed candidates.

The two leaders were formally appointed members of the commission following the resignations of PPP Senator Farooq H Naek and PML-N member Sheikh Aftab Ahmad. Bilawal will represent the treasury benches in the National Assembly, while Rana Sanaullah will represent the Senate.

The appointments follow months of reported dissatisfaction within the PPP over its inability to secure the commission’s approval for several candidates it had supported for judicial positions.

According to media reports, Senator Farooq H Naek had proposed 33 candidates for appointments to the high courts: 16 for the Sindh High Court, 10 for the Lahore High Court, five for the Balochistan High Court and two for the Islamabad High Court. These reports said the PPP failed to secure approval for its preferred candidates in the relevant deliberations.

Sources familiar with the latest political discussions now suggest that differences between the PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments have eased. They believe the evolving understanding between the coalition partners could provide an opportunity for some PPP-backed candidates to be reconsidered in future rounds of appointments.

However, the extent of any such understanding, and whether it includes agreement on specific candidates, remains unclear. There is also no public confirmation of such an understanding by the two parties.

Bilawal’s inclusion in the commission is particularly significant in the context of the PPP’s reported demand for a greater say in judicial appointments. The party had previously expressed dissatisfaction after its preferred candidates failed to obtain the necessary support, while its senior legal representative, Farooq H Naek, had proposed candidates for several high courts. Apparently for the same reason, the Presidency had recently delayed approval of many appointments. The commission’s composition has become an important factor in the debate over judicial appointments following constitutional changes that expanded parliamentary representation in the process. Its decisions, however, continue to depend on the commission’s voting procedure.

The JCP’s next meeting is scheduled for October 13, 2026, with the extension of the term of the Sindh High Court’s constitutional benches on the reported agenda.

Originally published in The News

Apparently for the same reason, the Presidency had recently delayed approval of many appointments. The commission’s composition has become an important factor in the debate over judicial appointments following constitutional changes that expanded parliamentary representation in the process. Its decisions, however, continue to depend on the commission’s voting procedure.
The JCP’s next meeting is scheduled for October 13, 2026, with the extension of the term of the Sindh High Court’s constitutional benches on the reported agenda.

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">People stand behind a crime scene tape. — AFP/File</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Police say victim died by suicide due to distress.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Victim's father sold plot to pay for her admission.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Police conducting autopsy to find out cause of death.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: A man suspected of supplying fake US university admission documents to International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI) graduate Laiba Ijaz has been arrested from Islamabad’s H-13 sector, sources said.</p><p>Laiba reportedly died by suicide after discovering that the documents provided by the agent were fraudulent.</p><style>

	</div><p>The suspect had rented a room in the area and was living in hiding, according to the sources.</p><p>They said investigators had also found evidence on his mobile phone of alleged online fraud and the blackmailing of women.</p><p>The suspect had previously worked in the Anti-Corruption Establishment in Quetta but was suspended, sources said. He had also worked for a company in Islamabad.</p><p>Laiba's body was reportedly found hanging by the roadside in Islamabad’s G-10 sector, within the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.</p><p>According to police, she was distressed after discovering that the documents provided by an agent for admission to a US university were fraudulent.</p><p>Laiba's family said she had completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further studies abroad.</p><p>The family said an immigration consultant had demanded Rs7 million to secure her admission to a US university. Laiba’s father, who lived with his family in a rented flat and sold milk on a motorcycle, sold his plot and paid Rs2.1 million in cash to the agent, they added.</p><p>The family said Laiba’s mother’s jewellery was also deposited with a bank to arrange the remaining amount.</p><p>When Laiba had the admission documents checked, she discovered that they were fake, according to her family.</p><p>She sent a final message to her maternal uncle, saying: “Do not tell my father about the fraud committed against me. He will die.”</p><p>Police had said they were investigating the case from different angles and were awaiting Laiba’s post-mortem report to establish the cause of death.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">PM Shehbaz takes notice</span></h2><p>Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken notice of the alleged suicide of Laiba, describing the incident as extremely tragic, the PM's Office said.</p><p>The premier directed the Islamabad inspector general of police and chief commissioner to immediately arrest the suspect accused of defrauding the student.</p><p>He said the suspect would be given exemplary punishment in accordance with the law.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

<h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Interior ministry orders FIA action</span></h2><p>Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the interior ministry took notice of the incident and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take immediate action.</p><p>He said the student was defrauded and authorities ordered action against those responsible.</p><p>The FIA director general was working on the case, while the FIA director had also met the victim's parents, he added. The minister said those involved in the incident would be brought to justice.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">FIA begins probe</span></h2><p>The probe agency has launched an initial inquiry into the alleged suicide of Laiba, FIA Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari said.</p><p>Describing the matter as serious, Bukhari said a case would be registered after the inquiry.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

<p>He said the suspect allegedly defrauded Laiba of Rs7.2 million on the pretext of securing her admission to a university abroad and also took Rs500,000 from her brother on the promise of arranging a job.</p><p>According to the FIA director, the suspect would pose as an employee of the Supreme Court or an officer of a government institution.</p><p>Bukhari said Laiba had planned to surprise her family on October 12 with news of her admission to Harvard University. However, two days earlier, she had the university registration certificate checked and discovered that it was fake, he added.</p><p>The FIA director also confirmed that Laiba had sent her final message to her maternal uncle.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: Laiba Ijaz case: Suspect arrested from H-13; evidence of online fraud, blackmail emerges
subheadline: Gold medallist IIUI student allegedly died by suicide after discovering that her US university admission docs were fake
author: Ayaz Akbar Yousafzai, Azaz Syed, Duaa Mirza, Web Desk
article_text:
Police say victim died by suicide due to distress.
Victim's father sold plot to pay for her admission.
Police conducting autopsy to find out cause of death.

ISLAMABAD: A man suspected of supplying fake US university admission documents to International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI) graduate Laiba Ijaz has been arrested from Islamabad’s H-13 sector, sources said.

Laiba reportedly died by suicide after discovering that the documents provided by the agent were fraudulent.

The suspect had rented a room in the area and was living in hiding, according to the sources.

They said investigators had also found evidence on his mobile phone of alleged online fraud and the blackmailing of women.

The suspect had previously worked in the Anti-Corruption Establishment in Quetta but was suspended, sources said. He had also worked for a company in Islamabad.

Laiba's body was reportedly found hanging by the roadside in Islamabad’s G-10 sector, within the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.

According to police, she was distressed after discovering that the documents provided by an agent for admission to a US university were fraudulent.

Laiba's family said she had completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further studies abroad.

The family said an immigration consultant had demanded Rs7 million to secure her admission to a US university. Laiba’s father, who lived with his family in a rented flat and sold milk on a motorcycle, sold his plot and paid Rs2.1 million in cash to the agent, they added.

The family said Laiba’s mother’s jewellery was also deposited with a bank to arrange the remaining amount.

When Laiba had the admission documents checked, she discovered that they were fake, according to her family.

She sent a final message to her maternal uncle, saying: “Do not tell my father about the fraud committed against me. He will die.”

Police had said they were investigating the case from different angles and were awaiting Laiba’s post-mortem report to establish the cause of death.

PM Shehbaz takes notice

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken notice of the alleged suicide of Laiba, describing the incident as extremely tragic, the PM's Office said.

The premier directed the Islamabad inspector general of police and chief commissioner to immediately arrest the suspect accused of defrauding the student.

He said the suspect would be given exemplary punishment in accordance with the law.

Interior ministry orders FIA action

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the interior ministry took notice of the incident and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take immediate action.

He said the student was defrauded and authorities ordered action against those responsible.

The FIA director general was working on the case, while the FIA director had also met the victim's parents, he added. The minister said those involved in the incident would be brought to justice.

FIA begins probe

The probe agency has launched an initial inquiry into the alleged suicide of Laiba, FIA Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari said.

Describing the matter as serious, Bukhari said a case would be registered after the inquiry.

He said the suspect allegedly defrauded Laiba of Rs7.2 million on the pretext of securing her admission to a university abroad and also took Rs500,000 from her brother on the promise of arranging a job.

According to the FIA director, the suspect would pose as an employee of the Supreme Court or an officer of a government institution.

Bukhari said Laiba had planned to surprise her family on October 12 with news of her admission to Harvard University. However, two days earlier, she had the university registration certificate checked and discovered that it was fake, he added.

The FIA director also confirmed that Laiba had sent her final message to her maternal uncle.

article_html:
• Police say victim died by suicide due to distress.
  • Victim's father sold plot to pay for her admission.
  • Police conducting autopsy to find out cause of death.

ISLAMABAD: A man suspected of supplying fake US university admission documents to International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI) graduate Laiba Ijaz has been arrested from Islamabad’s H-13 sector, sources said.

Laiba reportedly died by suicide after discovering that the documents provided by the agent were fraudulent.

The suspect had rented a room in the area and was living in hiding, according to the sources.

They said investigators had also found evidence on his mobile phone of alleged online fraud and the blackmailing of women.

The suspect had previously worked in the Anti-Corruption Establishment in Quetta but was suspended, sources said. He had also worked for a company in Islamabad.

Laiba's body was reportedly found hanging by the roadside in Islamabad’s G-10 sector, within the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.

According to police, she was distressed after discovering that the documents provided by an agent for admission to a US university were fraudulent.

Laiba's family said she had completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further studies abroad.

The family said an immigration consultant had demanded Rs7 million to secure her admission to a US university. Laiba’s father, who lived with his family in a rented flat and sold milk on a motorcycle, sold his plot and paid Rs2.1 million in cash to the agent, they added.

The family said Laiba’s mother’s jewellery was also deposited with a bank to arrange the remaining amount.

When Laiba had the admission documents checked, she discovered that they were fake, according to her family.

She sent a final message to her maternal uncle, saying: “Do not tell my father about the fraud committed against me. He will die.”

Police had said they were investigating the case from different angles and were awaiting Laiba’s post-mortem report to establish the cause of death.

PM Shehbaz takes notice

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken notice of the alleged suicide of Laiba, describing the incident as extremely tragic, the PM's Office said.

The premier directed the Islamabad inspector general of police and chief commissioner to immediately arrest the suspect accused of defrauding the student.

He said the suspect would be given exemplary punishment in accordance with the law.

Interior ministry orders FIA action

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the interior ministry took notice of the incident and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take immediate action.

He said the student was defrauded and authorities ordered action against those responsible.

The FIA director general was working on the case, while the FIA director had also met the victim's parents, he added. The minister said those involved in the incident would be brought to justice.

FIA begins probe

The probe agency has launched an initial inquiry into the alleged suicide of Laiba, FIA Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari said.

Describing the matter as serious, Bukhari said a case would be registered after the inquiry.

He said the suspect allegedly defrauded Laiba of Rs7.2 million on the pretext of securing her admission to a university abroad and also took Rs500,000 from her brother on the promise of arranging a job.

According to the FIA director, the suspect would pose as an employee of the Supreme Court or an officer of a government institution.

Bukhari said Laiba had planned to surprise her family on October 12 with news of her admission to Harvard University. However, two days earlier, she had the university registration certificate checked and discovered that it was fake, he added.

The FIA director also confirmed that Laiba had sent her final message to her maternal uncle.

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">Human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari (right) with her husband and fellow lawyer Hadi Ali Chattha, during a court hearing in Islamabad on December 5, 2025. — AFP</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Imaan, Hadi produced before court via video link.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">ATC records three prosecution witnesses' statements.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Judge Sipra adjourns proceedings until Monday.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Saturday disposed of a petition challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in a security breach case registered against lawyer and human rights activist Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha.</p><p>The case, registered at Aabpara Police Station, stems from allegations that the couple posed a security risk by interfering in state affairs during the visit of an international cricket team in October 2024.</p><style>

	</div><p>The ATC in Islamabad indicted Mazari and Chattha in the case earlier this week despite the accused objecting that they had not yet received copies of the case documents.</p><p>During today's proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra questioned why the accused had not been produced before the court despite an order directing their appearance in person or through video link.</p><p>The judge directed court staff to contact Adiala jail authorities to establish why the two accused had not been brought to court. No jail official appeared before the court during the hearing.</p><p>The court subsequently sought a report from the jail authorities and briefly suspended proceedings to establish the circumstances surrounding the failure to produce the accused.</p><p>The couple was later produced via video link, where Chattha questioned why the two had not been produced before the court.</p><p>According to Chattha, they had learnt from newspaper reports the following day that charges had been framed against them in the case.</p><p>Judge Sipra responded that the accused had challenged the framing of charges, saying the high court would set aside the charge if it had not been framed correctly.</p><p>The judge also directed a jail official to submit an explanation for failing to produce Mazari and Chattha, saying the court had ordered their appearance.</p><p>The court disposed of an application challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in the case, with Judge Sipra saying the application could not be heard at the current stage of the proceedings.</p><p>The application was disposed of without hearing the defence lawyers.</p><p>Defence counsel Zainab Janjua said the accused had not been present before the court in person or via video link during the open-court proceedings.</p><p>Janjua alleged that Mazari and Chattha were being deprived of their right to a fair trial, and boycotted the proceedings along with the accused.</p><p>Following the boycott, the court proceeded with the trial in the absence of the couple and their defence lawyers, recording statements from three prosecution witnesses.</p><p>The court summoned further witnesses for Monday and adjourned the hearing until then.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Rearrest</span></h2><p>The lawyer couple has been in custody since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them over a protest outside the Islamabad High Court.</p><p>A day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case related to controversial social media posts.</p><p>On September 17, following months of proceedings, the Supreme Court suspended the couple's sentences in a case related to controversial tweets and granted them bail against surety bonds worth Rs200,000 each, until the final decision on the case pending before the Islamabad High Court.</p><p>However, the relief was short-lived. Hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court (ATC).</p><p>According to the FIR, Mazari and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads during a protest.</p>                    </div>

headline: ATC disposes of Imaan, Hadi's plea against terrorism provisions in security breach case
subheadline: Islamabad court proceeded with the trial in couple's absence after their defence lawyers boycott proceedings
author: Arfa Feroz Zake
article_text:
Imaan, Hadi produced before court via video link.
ATC records three prosecution witnesses' statements.
Judge Sipra adjourns proceedings until Monday.

ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Saturday disposed of a petition challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in a security breach case registered against lawyer and human rights activist Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha.

The case, registered at Aabpara Police Station, stems from allegations that the couple posed a security risk by interfering in state affairs during the visit of an international cricket team in October 2024.

The ATC in Islamabad indicted Mazari and Chattha in the case earlier this week despite the accused objecting that they had not yet received copies of the case documents.

During today's proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra questioned why the accused had not been produced before the court despite an order directing their appearance in person or through video link.

The judge directed court staff to contact Adiala jail authorities to establish why the two accused had not been brought to court. No jail official appeared before the court during the hearing.

The court subsequently sought a report from the jail authorities and briefly suspended proceedings to establish the circumstances surrounding the failure to produce the accused.

The couple was later produced via video link, where Chattha questioned why the two had not been produced before the court.

According to Chattha, they had learnt from newspaper reports the following day that charges had been framed against them in the case.

Judge Sipra responded that the accused had challenged the framing of charges, saying the high court would set aside the charge if it had not been framed correctly.

The judge also directed a jail official to submit an explanation for failing to produce Mazari and Chattha, saying the court had ordered their appearance.

The court disposed of an application challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in the case, with Judge Sipra saying the application could not be heard at the current stage of the proceedings.

The application was disposed of without hearing the defence lawyers.

Defence counsel Zainab Janjua said the accused had not been present before the court in person or via video link during the open-court proceedings.

Janjua alleged that Mazari and Chattha were being deprived of their right to a fair trial, and boycotted the proceedings along with the accused.

Following the boycott, the court proceeded with the trial in the absence of the couple and their defence lawyers, recording statements from three prosecution witnesses.

The court summoned further witnesses for Monday and adjourned the hearing until then.

Rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in custody since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them over a protest outside the Islamabad High Court.

A day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case related to controversial social media posts.

On September 17, following months of proceedings, the Supreme Court suspended the couple's sentences in a case related to controversial tweets and granted them bail against surety bonds worth Rs200,000 each, until the final decision on the case pending before the Islamabad High Court.

However, the relief was short-lived. Hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court (ATC).

According to the FIR, Mazari and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads during a protest.

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="" spellcheck="false">President Asif Ali Zardari (fourth left), Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif (fourth right) and others present during a meeting in Islamabad on October 10, 2026. — PID</figcaption><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><superhuman-go-underlines data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; display: contents; --rem: 16;"></superhuman-go-underlines></figure></div><ul><li><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Cabinet meeting scheduled for Sunday morning: sources. </span></li><li><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">NA and Senate sessions to be summoned on Oct 13.</span></li><li><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Section 144 imposed across Rawalpindi for one month.<br></span></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>The federal government has decided to impose an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march towards Islamabad, said well-informed sources on Saturday.</p><p>The development came during a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-e-Sadr. </p><style>

	</div><p>The premier was accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and others.  </p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

</div>
<p>PPP’s Senator Sherry Rehman, Syed Naveed Qamar, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Dr Asim Hussain were also present on the occasion.</p><p>“It was agreed in the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and Senate on October 13,” read a statement issued by the President House.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2108903972182298913" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>

</div>
<p>The insiders said that the federal cabinet meeting sought for 9:30am on Sunday to approve emergency in KP. </p><p>Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz telephoned Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) Chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and congratulated him on performing Umrah.</p><p>The PM invited the JUI-F chief to a meeting at the Prime Minister’s House, which the latter accepted.</p><p>During the meeting, the JUI-F chief once again suggested to the premier to hold talks with PTI to end the ongoing political crisis in the country.  </p><p>He suggested resolving the issue through negotiations rather than imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the insiders added. </p><p>He reiterated his support for meaningful talks between the government and the PTI to find a way forward.</p><p>The prime minister briefed the JUI-F chief in detail on the government’s efforts to engage in dialogue with the opposition. </p><p>PM Shehbaz said the government was making every possible effort to resolve the matter through mutual understanding, sources added.</p><p>The JUI-F chief urged the prime minister to take his party’s core committee into confidence over the matter.</p><p>He has sought more time from the PM to consult the opposition and PTI on resolving the ongoing political impasse, the sources added.</p><p>The JUI-F chief, later, contacted opposition leaders and the PTI leadership in Islamabad.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Federal cabinet to decide on KP emergency </span></h2><p>Speaking on <span style="font-style: italic;">Geo News</span> programme 'Naya Pakistan', KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said that no official decision has been taken on imposing an emergency or governor's rule in the province.</p><p>The governor said that said the federal cabinet would decide on Sunday whether to impose an emergency, governor's rule or both.</p><p>The governor also criticised KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying he should resign if he could not protect the people of his province.</p><p>Responding to a question, Kundi ruled out the possibility of further talks with the province's ruling party, the PTI. </p><p>The governor said several PTI members were either under arrest or surrendering themselves.</p><p>He alleged that the party did not want dialogue and questioned whether it could be considered a political party. Kundi further accused the PTI of engaging in talks only through confrontation and unrest.</p><h2>No room left to avoid emergency: Naqvi </h2><p>Severalty, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that there appears to be little room left to avoid an emergency, responding to a journalist’s question during an informal conversation with reporters.</p><p>"Is there any room left for an emergency not to be imposed?" Naqvi remarked in response to a question.</p><p>The interior minister asked them to suggest how the situation could be averted. He urged them to ask the relevant parties how many efforts he had made to find a solution.</p><p>"They themselves will tell you how far I went in my efforts to resolve the matter," Naqvi said.</p><p>The interior minister added that no room for further options remained, according to his informal remarks to journalists.</p><h2>Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi for one month </h2><p>Section 144 has been imposed across Rawalpindi district for one month, from October 10 to November 8, according to an official notification.</p><p>Under the notification, public gatherings, rallies, processions, sit-ins and protests have been banned. The gathering of five or more people is also prohibited.</p><p>The restrictions further ban carrying weapons, sticks and petrol bombs. Double riding on motorcycles and the use of loudspeakers have also been prohibited.</p><p>According to the notification, Section 144 has been enforced in view of security concerns across the district.</p><p>Legal action will be taken against those found violating the restrictions, the notification stated.</p><p>PTI-led KP government and the federal government have been odds over various issues, particularly on the counter-terrorism policy. The federal government has repeatedly asked the PTI and the provincial government in KP to shun “extremist” politics and back the Centre’s anti-terrorism policy but has failed to receive a clear, positive response.</p><p>In addition to this, the Imran Khan founded-parity, on October 4, launched a protest march towards the federal capital aimed at seeking the release of its jailed founding chairman Khan and what it describes as the restoration of constitutional supremacy.</p><p>Khan, who has been in jail since August 2023, faces multiple cases ranging from corruption to terrorism since his ouster from power via the opposition's no-trust motion in April 2022.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: Federal govt decides to impose emergency in KP: sources
subheadline: Cabinet to consider proposal tomorrow; separate National Assembly and Senate sessions to be held on Oct 13
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Cabinet meeting scheduled for Sunday morning: sources.
NA and Senate sessions to be summoned on Oct 13.
Section 144 imposed across Rawalpindi for one month.

The federal government has decided to impose an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march towards Islamabad, said well-informed sources on Saturday.

The development came during a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-e-Sadr.

The premier was accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and others.

PPP’s Senator Sherry Rehman, Syed Naveed Qamar, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Dr Asim Hussain were also present on the occasion.

“It was agreed in the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and Senate on October 13,” read a statement issued by the President House.

The insiders said that the federal cabinet meeting sought for 9:30am on Sunday to approve emergency in KP.

Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz telephoned Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) Chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and congratulated him on performing Umrah.

The PM invited the JUI-F chief to a meeting at the Prime Minister’s House, which the latter accepted.

During the meeting, the JUI-F chief once again suggested to the premier to hold talks with PTI to end the ongoing political crisis in the country.

He suggested resolving the issue through negotiations rather than imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the insiders added.

He reiterated his support for meaningful talks between the government and the PTI to find a way forward.

The prime minister briefed the JUI-F chief in detail on the government’s efforts to engage in dialogue with the opposition.

PM Shehbaz said the government was making every possible effort to resolve the matter through mutual understanding, sources added.

The JUI-F chief urged the prime minister to take his party’s core committee into confidence over the matter.

He has sought more time from the PM to consult the opposition and PTI on resolving the ongoing political impasse, the sources added.

The JUI-F chief, later, contacted opposition leaders and the PTI leadership in Islamabad.

Federal cabinet to decide on KP emergency

Speaking on Geo News programme 'Naya Pakistan', KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said that no official decision has been taken on imposing an emergency or governor's rule in the province.

The governor said that said the federal cabinet would decide on Sunday whether to impose an emergency, governor's rule or both.

The governor also criticised KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying he should resign if he could not protect the people of his province.

Responding to a question, Kundi ruled out the possibility of further talks with the province's ruling party, the PTI.

The governor said several PTI members were either under arrest or surrendering themselves.

He alleged that the party did not want dialogue and questioned whether it could be considered a political party. Kundi further accused the PTI of engaging in talks only through confrontation and unrest.

No room left to avoid emergency: Naqvi

Severalty, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that there appears to be little room left to avoid an emergency, responding to a journalist’s question during an informal conversation with reporters.

"Is there any room left for an emergency not to be imposed?" Naqvi remarked in response to a question.

The interior minister asked them to suggest how the situation could be averted. He urged them to ask the relevant parties how many efforts he had made to find a solution.

"They themselves will tell you how far I went in my efforts to resolve the matter," Naqvi said.

The interior minister added that no room for further options remained, according to his informal remarks to journalists.

Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi for one month

Section 144 has been imposed across Rawalpindi district for one month, from October 10 to November 8, according to an official notification.

Under the notification, public gatherings, rallies, processions, sit-ins and protests have been banned. The gathering of five or more people is also prohibited.

The restrictions further ban carrying weapons, sticks and petrol bombs. Double riding on motorcycles and the use of loudspeakers have also been prohibited.

According to the notification, Section 144 has been enforced in view of security concerns across the district.

Legal action will be taken against those found violating the restrictions, the notification stated.

PTI-led KP government and the federal government have been odds over various issues, particularly on the counter-terrorism policy. The federal government has repeatedly asked the PTI and the provincial government in KP to shun “extremist” politics and back the Centre’s anti-terrorism policy but has failed to receive a clear, positive response.

In addition to this, the Imran Khan founded-parity, on October 4, launched a protest march towards the federal capital aimed at seeking the release of its jailed founding chairman Khan and what it describes as the restoration of constitutional supremacy.

Khan, who has been in jail since August 2023, faces multiple cases ranging from corruption to terrorism since his ouster from power via the opposition's no-trust motion in April 2022.

article_html:
• Cabinet meeting scheduled for Sunday morning: sources. 
  • NA and Senate sessions to be summoned on Oct 13.
  • Section 144 imposed across Rawalpindi for one month.

The federal government has decided to impose an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march towards Islamabad, said well-informed sources on Saturday.

The development came during a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-e-Sadr.

The premier was accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and others.

PPP’s Senator Sherry Rehman, Syed Naveed Qamar, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Dr Asim Hussain were also present on the occasion.

“It was agreed in the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and Senate on October 13,” read a statement issued by the President House.

The insiders said that the federal cabinet meeting sought for 9:30am on Sunday to approve emergency in KP.

Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz telephoned Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) Chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and congratulated him on performing Umrah.

The PM invited the JUI-F chief to a meeting at the Prime Minister’s House, which the latter accepted.

During the meeting, the JUI-F chief once again suggested to the premier to hold talks with PTI to end the ongoing political crisis in the country.

He suggested resolving the issue through negotiations rather than imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the insiders added.

He reiterated his support for meaningful talks between the government and the PTI to find a way forward.

The prime minister briefed the JUI-F chief in detail on the government’s efforts to engage in dialogue with the opposition.

PM Shehbaz said the government was making every possible effort to resolve the matter through mutual understanding, sources added.

The JUI-F chief urged the prime minister to take his party’s core committee into confidence over the matter.

He has sought more time from the PM to consult the opposition and PTI on resolving the ongoing political impasse, the sources added.

The JUI-F chief, later, contacted opposition leaders and the PTI leadership in Islamabad.

Federal cabinet to decide on KP emergency

Speaking on Geo News programme 'Naya Pakistan', KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said that no official decision has been taken on imposing an emergency or governor's rule in the province.

The governor said that said the federal cabinet would decide on Sunday whether to impose an emergency, governor's rule or both.

The governor also criticised KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying he should resign if he could not protect the people of his province.

Responding to a question, Kundi ruled out the possibility of further talks with the province's ruling party, the PTI.

The governor said several PTI members were either under arrest or surrendering themselves.

He alleged that the party did not want dialogue and questioned whether it could be considered a political party. Kundi further accused the PTI of engaging in talks only through confrontation and unrest.

No room left to avoid emergency: Naqvi

Severalty, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that there appears to be little room left to avoid an emergency, responding to a journalist’s question during an informal conversation with reporters.

"Is there any room left for an emergency not to be imposed?" Naqvi remarked in response to a question.

The interior minister asked them to suggest how the situation could be averted. He urged them to ask the relevant parties how many efforts he had made to find a solution.

"They themselves will tell you how far I went in my efforts to resolve the matter," Naqvi said.

The interior minister added that no room for further options remained, according to his informal remarks to journalists.

Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi for one month

Section 144 has been imposed across Rawalpindi district for one month, from October 10 to November 8, according to an official notification.

Under the notification, public gatherings, rallies, processions, sit-ins and protests have been banned. The gathering of five or more people is also prohibited.

The restrictions further ban carrying weapons, sticks and petrol bombs. Double riding on motorcycles and the use of loudspeakers have also been prohibited.

According to the notification, Section 144 has been enforced in view of security concerns across the district.

Legal action will be taken against those found violating the restrictions, the notification stated.

PTI-led KP government and the federal government have been odds over various issues, particularly on the counter-terrorism policy. The federal government has repeatedly asked the PTI and the provincial government in KP to shun “extremist” politics and back the Centre’s anti-terrorism policy but has failed to receive a clear, positive response.

In addition to this, the Imran Khan founded-parity, on October 4, launched a protest march towards the federal capital aimed at seeking the release of its jailed founding chairman Khan and what it describes as the restoration of constitutional supremacy.

Khan, who has been in jail since August 2023, faces multiple cases ranging from corruption to terrorism since his ouster from power via the opposition's no-trust motion in April 2022.

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">A Pakistani police officer stands guard outside the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Islamabad on January 18, 2024. — AFP</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b>Islamabad urges world to condemn attacks on civilian infrastructure.</b></li><li><b>FO expresses concern over casualties, extends condolences to families.</b></li><li><b>Pakistan pledges continued support for Saudi security.<br></b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Sunday strongly condemned Houthi militia attack targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirming Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.</p><p>At least 12 people were killed and 309 wounded in a Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, Saudi authorities said, as the Iran-backed group escalated its campaign against the kingdom.</p><style>

	</div><p>The dead included four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and one person each from the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, according to the Saudi civil aviation authority.</p><p>In a statement, the prime minister condemned what he called a “heinous attack” and extended condolences to the bereaved families, while praying for the swift and full recovery of those injured.</p><p>“Attacks targeting civilians and critical infrastructure are completely unacceptable and constitute a serious threat to regional peace and stability,” Shehbaz said, adding that such acts of violence, which constitute a flagrant violation of international law, must cease immediately.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2109110050627129720" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>He reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with Saudi Arabia, its leadership and its people, citing the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the enduring bonds of brotherhood between the two countries.</p><p>“We reaffirm our steadfast commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security,” the prime minister said.</p><p>Separately, the Foreign Office (FO) strongly condemned the latest terrorist attack by the Houthi militia, describing the targeting of a civilian airport as a heinous act of terrorism, a flagrant violation of international law and a grave threat to regional peace and security.</p><p>The FO expressed profound concern over reports of casualties and injuries resulting from the attack. It extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured a swift and complete recovery, saying its prayers were with the victims and their families.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2109116439781400628" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>“The continued targeting of civilian population and critical infrastructure by the Houthi militia is utterly unacceptable and must be condemned unequivocally by the international community,” the FO said.</p><p>It added that such “brazen and indiscriminate acts of aggression” could not be justified under any circumstances and must cease immediately.</p><p>The Foreign Office said Pakistan stood in unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the face of repeated terrorist attacks.</p><p>“In accordance with the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence and the recent decisions taken by its Strategic, Political and Defence Committee, Pakistan reiterates its firm and unshakeable commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the statement said.</p><p>The FO also said Pakistan fully supported Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to defend its territory, protect its people and safeguard its cities and vital infrastructure against all threats and acts of aggression.</p><p>Calling for an immediate halt to the attacks, Pakistan urged the Houthi militia to cease its terrorist activities and called on the international community to take a firm and unequivocal stand against acts that endangered innocent lives and undermined regional stability.</p><p>“Pakistan will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, resolute in its commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, security and defence,” the Foreign Office said.</p><p>The Foreign Office statement came days after Islamabad, Riyadh and Ankara agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.</p><p>The three nations took the decision at an emergency meeting of the MJDA in Riyadh, the Foreign Office said on October 6, adding that it would be carried out under "approved arrangements" and the national laws of the three countries.</p><p>Later that day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif confirmed that Pakistan and Turkiye have been providing support to Saudi Arabia in its operations against Houthis in Yemen.</p><p></p><hr class="editorHr"><p></p><p><i>— With headline: Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, reaffirms commitment to Saudi security
subheadline: FO says targeting of civilian airport by Houthi militia constitutes heinous act of terrorism and grave threat to regional peace
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Islamabad urges world to condemn attacks on civilian infrastructure.
FO expresses concern over casualties, extends condolences to families.
Pakistan pledges continued support for Saudi security.

ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Sunday strongly condemned Houthi militia attack targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirming Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.

At least 12 people were killed and 309 wounded in a Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, Saudi authorities said, as the Iran-backed group escalated its campaign against the kingdom.

The dead included four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and one person each from the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, according to the Saudi civil aviation authority.

In a statement, the prime minister condemned what he called a “heinous attack” and extended condolences to the bereaved families, while praying for the swift and full recovery of those injured.

“Attacks targeting civilians and critical infrastructure are completely unacceptable and constitute a serious threat to regional peace and stability,” Shehbaz said, adding that such acts of violence, which constitute a flagrant violation of international law, must cease immediately.

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with Saudi Arabia, its leadership and its people, citing the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the enduring bonds of brotherhood between the two countries.

“We reaffirm our steadfast commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security,” the prime minister said.

Separately, the Foreign Office (FO) strongly condemned the latest terrorist attack by the Houthi militia, describing the targeting of a civilian airport as a heinous act of terrorism, a flagrant violation of international law and a grave threat to regional peace and security.

The FO expressed profound concern over reports of casualties and injuries resulting from the attack. It extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured a swift and complete recovery, saying its prayers were with the victims and their families.

“The continued targeting of civilian population and critical infrastructure by the Houthi militia is utterly unacceptable and must be condemned unequivocally by the international community,” the FO said.

It added that such “brazen and indiscriminate acts of aggression” could not be justified under any circumstances and must cease immediately.

The Foreign Office said Pakistan stood in unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the face of repeated terrorist attacks.

“In accordance with the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence and the recent decisions taken by its Strategic, Political and Defence Committee, Pakistan reiterates its firm and unshakeable commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the statement said.

The FO also said Pakistan fully supported Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to defend its territory, protect its people and safeguard its cities and vital infrastructure against all threats and acts of aggression.

Calling for an immediate halt to the attacks, Pakistan urged the Houthi militia to cease its terrorist activities and called on the international community to take a firm and unequivocal stand against acts that endangered innocent lives and undermined regional stability.

“Pakistan will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, resolute in its commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, security and defence,” the Foreign Office said.

The Foreign Office statement came days after Islamabad, Riyadh and Ankara agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.

The three nations took the decision at an emergency meeting of the MJDA in Riyadh, the Foreign Office said on October 6, adding that it would be carried out under "approved arrangements" and the national laws of the three countries.

Later that day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif confirmed that Pakistan and Turkiye have been providing support to Saudi Arabia in its operations against Houthis in Yemen.

— With additional input from Reuters

In a statement, the prime minister condemned what he called a “heinous attack” and extended condolences to the bereaved families, while praying for the swift and full recovery of those injured.

“Attacks targeting civilians and critical infrastructure are completely unacceptable and constitute a serious threat to regional peace and stability,” Shehbaz said, adding that such acts of violence, which constitute a flagrant violation of international law, must cease immediately.

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with Saudi Arabia, its leadership and its people, citing the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the enduring bonds of brotherhood between the two countries.
“We reaffirm our steadfast commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security,” the prime minister said.

Separately, the Foreign Office (FO) strongly condemned the latest terrorist attack by the Houthi militia, describing the targeting of a civilian airport as a heinous act of terrorism, a flagrant violation of international law and a grave threat to regional peace and security.

The FO expressed profound concern over reports of casualties and injuries resulting from the attack. It extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured a swift and complete recovery, saying its prayers were with the victims and their families.

“The continued targeting of civilian population and critical infrastructure by the Houthi militia is utterly unacceptable and must be condemned unequivocally by the international community,” the FO said.
It added that such “brazen and indiscriminate acts of aggression” could not be justified under any circumstances and must cease immediately.
The Foreign Office said Pakistan stood in unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the face of repeated terrorist attacks.

“In accordance with the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence and the recent decisions taken by its Strategic, Political and Defence Committee, Pakistan reiterates its firm and unshakeable commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the statement said.

The FO also said Pakistan fully supported Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to defend its territory, protect its people and safeguard its cities and vital infrastructure against all threats and acts of aggression.

Calling for an immediate halt to the attacks, Pakistan urged the Houthi militia to cease its terrorist activities and called on the international community to take a firm and unequivocal stand against acts that endangered innocent lives and undermined regional stability.
“Pakistan will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, resolute in its commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, security and defence,” the Foreign Office said.
The Foreign Office statement came days after Islamabad, Riyadh and Ankara agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.

The three nations took the decision at an emergency meeting of the MJDA in Riyadh, the Foreign Office said on October 6, adding that it would be carried out under "approved arrangements" and the national laws of the three countries.
Later that day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif confirmed that Pakistan and Turkiye have been providing support to Saudi Arabia in its operations against Houthis in Yemen.
— With additional input from Reuters

                                <div class="heading_H"><h1>12 terrorists, Afghan Taliban personnel killed as security forces foil infiltration bid in Kurram</h1></div>

                        <h2>Soldier embraces martyrdom during intense exchange of fire with Indian-sponsored terrorists, says ISPR</h2>
                    </div>

	</div><p>A soldier was martyred while 12 Fitna al-Khawarij and Afghan Taliban personnel were killed during an attempted infiltration from Afghanistan into Kurram district, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.</p><p>The movement of a group of khwarij attempting to approach the international border from Afghanistan was detected on October 10, following which security forces effectively engaged them, the military's media wing said in a statement issued on October 11.</p><p>Despite maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, security forces faced firing from Afghan Taliban posts, which opened fire to support the infiltration attempt, the ISPR said.</p><p>It added that skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of 12 khwarij and Afghan Taliban personnel.</p><p>However, Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, 40, a resident of Ghizer district, embraced martyrdom during the intense exchange of fire.</p><p>The ISPR said the incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border once again vindicated Pakistan's stance regarding the Afghan Taliban regime's failure to prevent terrorist organisations from using Afghan soil, alleging that the regime instead facilitated and patronised cross-border terrorism.</p><p>The military's media wing added that the Afghan Taliban regime had consistently failed to fulfil its international counter-terrorism obligations.</p><p>A sanitisation operation is under way in the area to eliminate any remaining Indian-sponsored khwarij, the statement said.</p><p>Reaffirming its commitment to defending the country's frontiers, the ISPR said security forces and law enforcement agencies would continue their counter-terrorism campaign under the "Azm-e-Istehkam" vision, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, to eliminate foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.</p><p>The statement said the sacrifices of security personnel further reinforced Pakistan's commitment to safeguarding the nation and its frontiers at all costs.</p><p>The development comes two days after forces killed seven Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district.</p><p>The IBO was carried out against India-backed militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, with several hideouts also destroyed, the ISPR said.</p><p>Pakistan has witnessed a sharp rise in cross-border terrorist incidents, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in 2021.</p><p>Pakistan recorded its highest monthly number of militant attacks in 12 years during September 2026.</p><p>According to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring anti-state violence in the region, 225 militant attacks were recorded across the country in September, compared with 199 in August — an increase of 13%. Militant attacks increased for the third consecutive month.</p><p>Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent its territory from being used by militant organisations to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.</p><p>Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban authorities have failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.</p><p>Despite multiple rounds of talks, Islamabad and Kabul have yet to resolve their differences, with the issue of militant groups operating from Afghan soil remaining a major point of contention between the two sides.</p>                    </div>

headline: 12 terrorists, Afghan Taliban personnel killed as security forces foil infiltration bid in Kurram
subheadline: Soldier embraces martyrdom during intense exchange of fire with Indian-sponsored terrorists, says ISPR
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Naib Subedar Aman embraces martyrdom in intense border firefight.
ISPR says sanitisation operation targets remaining khwarij.
Afghan Taliban regime facilitating cross-border terrorism: ISPR

A soldier was martyred while 12 Fitna al-Khawarij and Afghan Taliban personnel were killed during an attempted infiltration from Afghanistan into Kurram district, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.

The movement of a group of khwarij attempting to approach the international border from Afghanistan was detected on October 10, following which security forces effectively engaged them, the military's media wing said in a statement issued on October 11.

Despite maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, security forces faced firing from Afghan Taliban posts, which opened fire to support the infiltration attempt, the ISPR said.

It added that skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of 12 khwarij and Afghan Taliban personnel.

However, Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, 40, a resident of Ghizer district, embraced martyrdom during the intense exchange of fire.

The ISPR said the incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border once again vindicated Pakistan's stance regarding the Afghan Taliban regime's failure to prevent terrorist organisations from using Afghan soil, alleging that the regime instead facilitated and patronised cross-border terrorism.

The military's media wing added that the Afghan Taliban regime had consistently failed to fulfil its international counter-terrorism obligations.

A sanitisation operation is under way in the area to eliminate any remaining Indian-sponsored khwarij, the statement said.

Reaffirming its commitment to defending the country's frontiers, the ISPR said security forces and law enforcement agencies would continue their counter-terrorism campaign under the "Azm-e-Istehkam" vision, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, to eliminate foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

The statement said the sacrifices of security personnel further reinforced Pakistan's commitment to safeguarding the nation and its frontiers at all costs.

The development comes two days after forces killed seven Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district.

The IBO was carried out against India-backed militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, with several hideouts also destroyed, the ISPR said.

Pakistan has witnessed a sharp rise in cross-border terrorist incidents, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in 2021.

Pakistan recorded its highest monthly number of militant attacks in 12 years during September 2026.

According to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring anti-state violence in the region, 225 militant attacks were recorded across the country in September, compared with 199 in August — an increase of 13%. Militant attacks increased for the third consecutive month.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent its territory from being used by militant organisations to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.

Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban authorities have failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.

Despite multiple rounds of talks, Islamabad and Kabul have yet to resolve their differences, with the issue of militant groups operating from Afghan soil remaining a major point of contention between the two sides.

Despite maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, security forces faced firing from Afghan Taliban posts, which opened fire to support the infiltration attempt, the ISPR said.

It added that skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of 12 khwarij and Afghan Taliban personnel.

However, Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, 40, a resident of Ghizer district, embraced martyrdom during the intense exchange of fire.

The ISPR said the incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border once again vindicated Pakistan's stance regarding the Afghan Taliban regime's failure to prevent terrorist organisations from using Afghan soil, alleging that the regime instead facilitated and patronised cross-border terrorism.

The military's media wing added that the Afghan Taliban regime had consistently failed to fulfil its international counter-terrorism obligations.

A sanitisation operation is under way in the area to eliminate any remaining Indian-sponsored khwarij, the statement said.

Reaffirming its commitment to defending the country's frontiers, the ISPR said security forces and law enforcement agencies would continue their counter-terrorism campaign under the "Azm-e-Istehkam" vision, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, to eliminate foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

The statement said the sacrifices of security personnel further reinforced Pakistan's commitment to safeguarding the nation and its frontiers at all costs.

The development comes two days after forces killed seven Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district.

The IBO was carried out against India-backed militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, with several hideouts also destroyed, the ISPR said.

Pakistan has witnessed a sharp rise in cross-border terrorist incidents, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in 2021.

Pakistan recorded its highest monthly number of militant attacks in 12 years during September 2026.

According to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring anti-state violence in the region, 225 militant attacks were recorded across the country in September, compared with 199 in August — an increase of 13%. Militant attacks increased for the third consecutive month.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent its territory from being used by militant organisations to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.

Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban authorities have failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.

Despite multiple rounds of talks, Islamabad and Kabul have yet to resolve their differences, with the issue of militant groups operating from Afghan soil remaining a major point of contention between the two sides.

                                <div class="heading_H"><h1>PTI calls Centre's move to impose emergency in KP a 'grave political mistake'</h1></div>
                                    <div class="except" style="margin-bottom: 12px;">
                        <h2>PTI's Junaid Akbar claims he and CM Afridi have been arrested, but govt has yet to issue an official statement</h2>

<html><body><div class="medium-insert-images ui-sortable"><figure contenteditable="false">
    <img src="https://www.geo.tv/assets/uploads/updates/2026-10-11/686028_905059_updates.jpg" alt="PTI Chairman Gohar Khan talks to the media as he arrives to attend a hearing at the high court in Islamabad on August 29, 2023. — AFP" width="700" height="400" class="">

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="" spellcheck="false">PTI Chairman Gohar Khan talks to the media as he arrives to attend a hearing at the high court in Islamabad on August 29, 2023. — AFP</figcaption><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><superhuman-go-underlines data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; display: contents; --rem: 16;"></superhuman-go-underlines></figure></div><ul><li><b>President approves Centre's emergency recommendations.</b></li><li><b>Gohar says KP's electoral mandate must be respected.</b></li><li><b>Qaiser demands implementation of peace jirga resolution.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has condemned the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, calling the move a "grave political mistake".</p><p>The federal government decided to invoke emergency measures under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution following a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday. Later, President Asif Ali Zardari approved the cabinet’s recommendations.</p><style>

	<ins class="adsbygoogle"
