	<script>
	     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
	</script>
	</div><p>The Centre cited the deteriorating security situation and alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.</p><p>The move comes amid escalating tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration, with disagreements over counterterrorism cooperation, provincial authority and the party's ongoing long march towards Islamabad.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><iframe class="youtube-video" style="width:100%;height:350px;" src="//www.youtube.com/embed/zbnkQKLwFik" allowfullscreen=""></iframe></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>In a post on X, Gohar warned that the federal government's decision would undermine democratic rights and provincial autonomy.</p><p>Gohar said his party strongly condemned and completely rejected the decision, describing it as an undemocratic measure that the people would never accept.</p><p>He maintained that the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have a constitutional and legal right to their electoral mandate, arguing that peace and stability could not be achieved by disregarding that mandate, weakening provincial autonomy or creating confrontation between the federation and the province.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2109190073392701783" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>The PTI chairman said there was no disagreement over the need to eliminate terrorism, but warned that the fight against militancy could not be used to suppress public opinion, pursue political objectives or restrict the province's constitutional powers.</p><p>He stressed that terrorism could only be defeated through national unity and a joint strategy.</p><p>"Provinces cannot be weakened to strengthen the federation," Gohar said, adding that the solution to the country's problems lay in political wisdom, constitutional supremacy, meaningful dialogue and practical measures rather than force, confrontation and extraordinary steps.</p><p>He pledged that the PTI would raise its voice through every constitutional, legal and democratic forum to protect the public mandate, provincial autonomy and democratic rights.</p><p>The party chairman said strong provinces formed the foundation of a strong federation, while constitutional supremacy guaranteed a strong Pakistan.</p><p>Gohar urged the federal government to reconsider its decision, saying it could still be reversed within a few days. He called on the Centre to set aside its ego, recognise ground realities, accept legitimate demands and respect public sentiment.</p><p>He warned that persisting with the decision could inflict further political and economic damage on the country and undermine the democratic process. Reviewing political decisions, he added, was not a sign of weakness but a demonstration of wisdom in the national interest.</p><p>Separately, PTI leader Asad Qaiser also rejected governor's rule and emergency measures in KP, vowing to continue the party's constitutional and democratic struggle to protect the province’s rights.</p><p>In a post on X, Qaiser said his party strongly condemned both measures, adding that it always raised its voice against terrorism. He questioned the federal government's policies, saying they had contributed to the current situation.</p><p>Qaiser called for the implementation of the unanimous resolution adopted by the peace jirga, which he said had the support of all political parties. He stressed that it was unacceptable to disregard people’s fundamental rights and powers in important national matters.</p><p>Urging all political parties to speak up for KP's rights, the PTI leader described the proposed measures as an attack on the province's constitutional rights and vowed that the party would continue its constitutional and democratic struggle.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2109202912362815644" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>Meanwhile, PTI KP President Junaid Akbar claimed in a post on X that he and Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had been arrested.</p><p>However, the government has not issued an official statement regarding the reported arrests so far.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2109199167813808172" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>The development follows PTI's long march on Islamabad, led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, which began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed to produce an agreement.</p><p>The talks broke down over disagreements concerning counterterrorism cooperation in KP and access to jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, including a meeting with his personal doctor.</p><p>The government and opposition exchanged accusations over the failure of negotiations, while Afridi continued leading the march through the province.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
</body></html>

headline: PTI calls Centre's move to impose emergency in KP a 'grave political mistake'
subheadline: PTI's Junaid Akbar claims he and CM Afridi have been arrested, but govt has yet to issue an official statement
author: Web Desk
article_text:
President approves Centre's emergency recommendations.
Gohar says KP's electoral mandate must be respected.
Qaiser demands implementation of peace jirga resolution.

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has condemned the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, calling the move a "grave political mistake".

The federal government decided to invoke emergency measures under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution following a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday. Later, President Asif Ali Zardari approved the cabinet’s recommendations.

The Centre cited the deteriorating security situation and alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.

The move comes amid escalating tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration, with disagreements over counterterrorism cooperation, provincial authority and the party's ongoing long march towards Islamabad.

In a post on X, Gohar warned that the federal government's decision would undermine democratic rights and provincial autonomy.

Gohar said his party strongly condemned and completely rejected the decision, describing it as an undemocratic measure that the people would never accept.

He maintained that the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have a constitutional and legal right to their electoral mandate, arguing that peace and stability could not be achieved by disregarding that mandate, weakening provincial autonomy or creating confrontation between the federation and the province.

The PTI chairman said there was no disagreement over the need to eliminate terrorism, but warned that the fight against militancy could not be used to suppress public opinion, pursue political objectives or restrict the province's constitutional powers.

He stressed that terrorism could only be defeated through national unity and a joint strategy.

"Provinces cannot be weakened to strengthen the federation," Gohar said, adding that the solution to the country's problems lay in political wisdom, constitutional supremacy, meaningful dialogue and practical measures rather than force, confrontation and extraordinary steps.

He pledged that the PTI would raise its voice through every constitutional, legal and democratic forum to protect the public mandate, provincial autonomy and democratic rights.

The party chairman said strong provinces formed the foundation of a strong federation, while constitutional supremacy guaranteed a strong Pakistan.

Gohar urged the federal government to reconsider its decision, saying it could still be reversed within a few days. He called on the Centre to set aside its ego, recognise ground realities, accept legitimate demands and respect public sentiment.

He warned that persisting with the decision could inflict further political and economic damage on the country and undermine the democratic process. Reviewing political decisions, he added, was not a sign of weakness but a demonstration of wisdom in the national interest.

Separately, PTI leader Asad Qaiser also rejected governor's rule and emergency measures in KP, vowing to continue the party's constitutional and democratic struggle to protect the province’s rights.

In a post on X, Qaiser said his party strongly condemned both measures, adding that it always raised its voice against terrorism. He questioned the federal government's policies, saying they had contributed to the current situation.

Qaiser called for the implementation of the unanimous resolution adopted by the peace jirga, which he said had the support of all political parties. He stressed that it was unacceptable to disregard people’s fundamental rights and powers in important national matters.

Urging all political parties to speak up for KP's rights, the PTI leader described the proposed measures as an attack on the province's constitutional rights and vowed that the party would continue its constitutional and democratic struggle.

Meanwhile, PTI KP President Junaid Akbar claimed in a post on X that he and Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had been arrested.

However, the government has not issued an official statement regarding the reported arrests so far.

The development follows PTI's long march on Islamabad, led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, which began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed to produce an agreement.

The talks broke down over disagreements concerning counterterrorism cooperation in KP and access to jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, including a meeting with his personal doctor.

The government and opposition exchanged accusations over the failure of negotiations, while Afridi continued leading the march through the province.

KP emergency, governor's rule: Legal experts explain govt's constitutional powers

Legal experts discuss constitutional provisions, federal powers and the implications of emergency rule in KP

By
Web Desk

Updated Sunday Oct 11 2026

The federal government on Sunday imposed governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and emergency in 12 districts of the province — effectively ending the provincial government’s powers.

Legal experts weigh in on the constitutional provisions governing emergency rule, the extent of federal powers and the impact of the move on the province’s elected leadership.

‘Right decision, limited time’

— Supreme Court lawyer Haris Azmat

[Articles 232 and 234] are an integral part of the Constitution. In one form or the other, since 1973, the framers of the Constitution envisaged that such a matter would eventually arise, and in such a situation, the federal government would have to act.

So, first of all, it must be clear that the action taken is an absolute constitutional decision. When the federal government perceives that a law and order issue has arisen within a province, or there is an external threat, or an absolute failure of non-governance, it can intervene for a limited time and for a limited purpose.

To achieve this, the entire procedure was followed — cabinet approval, consultation with the president —and following that entire procedure, the federal government has taken this decision.

Of course, the provincial government would certainly want to challenge such matters, and the procedure is given in the Constitution that these matters will go to the Federal Constitutional Court, where they can file a petition, and the FCC can judicially review whether the decision was correct and whether the circumstances cited by the federal government for imposing the emergency existed in the province at that time or not.

Having said that, in my view, as a citizen of Pakistan as well, this decision is a very good decision, in the sense that the reports arriving — reports stating for a long time that there is an absolute failure on the part of the provincial government.

Secondly, severe problems of terrorism exist there, and the life of the ordinary person is going from bad to worse — meant that in such matters, if the federal government had not taken this decision, it would have been a constitutional failure on the part of the federal government to act.

In our legal terms, a term is used called “omission to act” — when you possess the legal power to improve the lives of the general public, to eliminate terrorism, to safeguard the integrity of the country, and yet you do not act, that is also an illegality on the part of the federal government.

Therefore, the federal government has taken this decision following the proper procedure. Yes, that said, this decision is not for four years, five years, or an unlimited period. As the name implies, these emergency procedures are for a limited time. You take action within a limited time, and when things are restored, the Constitution contains a similar mechanism to undo this procedure, which will also take a day, and the whole thing will be undone.

Often, when these emergency situations are imposed — for example, to eliminate terrorism, address external threats, or in the event of war — under these emergency provisions, the federal government has the right, for a very limited purpose, to suspend these provisions so that any law and order or war situation can be resolved.

Within these same provisions, the federal government can act. “Governor’s rule” is, as they say, a layman’s term. Under these provisions, the federal government has the power to instruct the provincial governor — since the provincial governor is the representative of the federal government, appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister — to execute specific tasks on our directions, such as controlling the police or giving directions to any department.

Now, from today onwards, ever since the emergency has been imposed, if two conflicting directions arrive— one from the provincial government and one from the federal government (let’s group the federal government and governor together, or assume a direction comes from the governor today to the IG Police)— whose word will the IG Police obey under the law? Under the law, the IG Police will obey the governor and/or the federal government today.

Similarly, the entire apparatus of the provincial government, including all provincial secretaries and provincial departments, if any conflicting opinion arises now, will listen to the federal government and the provincial government, and implementing their directions has now become their constitutional responsibility until this situation normalises and legal matters return to normal.

As soon as normalisation occurs, within a minute or a day, this entire emergency is lifted. So, just as the name implies, it is an emergency, done for a limited, emergent situation.

‘Chief minister has no power’

— Lawyer Hasan Raza Pasha

The provincial government cannot call [the federal government’s move] unconstitutional because it simply does not have the power. If anyone can call it unconstitutional, it can be the superior courts. Now, even in that, the restriction is that if the President of Pakistan considers that we have to suspend the fundamental rights under the Constitution — for example, Articles 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, and 24 — they have been given this power under Article 233: when an emergency is in force, during that period they can suspend these fundamental rights, which are Articles 15 to 24.

So when they can suspend these, then the High Courts or the Supreme Court cannot take up these matters or deal with them. Although the last provision of Article 232 gives the power to suspend the rest, you cannot suspend the articles relating to the High Courts.

On the other hand, powers were given in Article 233 to the government and the President to suspend the articles of fundamental rights. The reason for this [move being legal] is that the power given in the Constitution has been invoked by the federal government and the President of Pakistan.

And you look at how the entire mechanism was laid out: first, the governor’s report came; reports from various institutions were sent to the President of Pakistan, then a meeting took place in which parliamentarians were present, along with the President of Pakistan and the Prime Minister.

After that, a cabinet meeting was held in the morning, and the cabinet, after a long session, sent a summary to the President of Pakistan, who endorsed it. And the matter does not end just here. There is no second opinion about this: the moment the President of Pakistan put his signature on it, the proclamation order was issued, its enforcement took place, and the notification became just a formality.

Moving forward, it is written in Article 232 itself that the President of Pakistan must send this proclamation order to the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament), and both houses of Parliament must separately endorse it, and a timeframe was given, which was that they have to endorse it within 10 days.

So it will not be the case that we wait for Parliament’s endorsement; rather it has already been implemented, and formal endorsement has to be done by Parliament. Certainly, since PTI members are present there as opposition, they will present their stance, and they should; this is the beauty of Parliament. Similarly, the treasury benches will present their stance; there will be debates, but the deadline is 10 days.

Moreover, if we look at Article 234, initially a time of two months is given — it will remain in force for two months. And if the federal government thinks that the situation is still not normal, then before those two months end, it can get a resolution passed by Parliament and extend it for another two months, and ultimately it will remain for up to six months. This is in Article 234.

But if Article 232 has been invoked, then there is no timeframe in it, so you will read it alongside Article 235, and in Article 235 it is stated that when conditions become normal, and the federal government or the President of Pakistan consider that conditions are now normal, then they can lift the emergency.

The powers of the provincial government have ended, and the powers of the Chief Minister have also ended.

Previously, if a Chief Secretary had to be appointed — although it is appointed by the federal government, it is done in consultation with the Chief Minister — the first order made after the enforcement of the emergency was the transfer of the Chief Secretary and posting a new Chief Secretary from the federation, Dr Fakhar Alam.

So there is no endorsement by the Chief Minister anywhere. From this, you can gauge that the Chief Minister has no power. Yes, if the Assembly passes any such law, then Parliament has the power to undo it, and both houses of Parliament — the Senate and the National Assembly — can abolish it because it is written in these very articles, meaning in Chapter 10, that if the provincial government passes any conflicting law, the overriding effect will be held by the federal Majlis-e-Shoora.

And just as you see, recently the PTI government made an amendment to the Police Act, so now that amendment — although it is within the competence of the provincial assembly and the date has passed — the federal Parliament, meaning the Majlis-e-Shoora, can undo it, and the overriding effect will prevail with the federal parliament, the Majlis-e-Shoora, the National Assembly, and the Senate, and their legislation will prevail over the provincial assembly.

However, the Assembly has not been dissolved; there is no order to dissolve the Assembly, and the Assembly exists in its own capacity. And if, suppose, a situation arises that after two months or four months the emergency is lifted, then what will happen? Will a new Chief Minister come or a new cabinet come? Absolutely not.

The same Chief Minister who was there before the enforcement of the emergency, and the same cabinet, will take over. So they are held in abeyance, meaning they exist as they are, but they are powerless and have no authority. The Assembly exists, but the Assembly cannot make any legislation that is in conflict with the federal government.

‘Complete, decisive end to terrorism’

— Muhammad Ali, security analyst

At this time there are two fundamental reasons for this, [the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency], due to which our Head of State — who is also Pakistan's constitutional Commander-in-Chief and Head of the Province — has the responsibility to carefully and promptly review whether, if a single unit of a province, its resources, energies, and mandate are not only failing to be used for the safety and eradication of terrorism for the people of its province — which is also a criminal negligence — but on the other hand, all provincial resources are being used to destabilise other provinces and the federation, then definitely no responsible state and its leadership can permit this.

So I commend the President's prompt and timely action, and I believe that this is a very important responsibility fulfilled for the nation's strength and security, and the summary and proposal of the federal cabinet have been acted upon immediately.

So, I believe that one more thing that is very important to clarify is that giving this any political colour or finding political motives is not appropriate. 

The biggest reason why this emergency has come into effect is, unfortunately, the criminal negligence of the KP provincial government in failing to take timely and prompt steps to protect its people and citizens from the threat of terrorism.

I want to share some facts with you: there is a police force of approximately 125,000 in the KP province, out of which 17,000 personnel are deployed on protocol duties. Whereas, to enhance the capability of the Counter-Terrorism Department, the Federation provided them with funds of approximately Rs800 crore at various times.

But the total strength of the Counter-Terrorism Department of KP is only 3,300 personnel, out of which independent personnel are only 25, while protocol duty personnel number 17,000.

So this is proof that, you feel it looks as though, unfortunately, the provincial government of KP completely lacked priority and interest in making its capability, personnel, and capacity effective in order to protect its public from terrorism and eliminate it, due to which—you could say—coercively, the President and the federal cabinet had to take this step in summary.

However, I hope that no attempt will be made to give it a political colour, but rather it will be considered a prompt and necessary step by the state and federal government, whose fundamental purpose is the protection of the lives, property, and honour of our millions of brothers and sisters in KP, and a complete and decisive end to terrorism.

'Constitutional'

— Lawyer Sheikh Saqib Ahmed

The President’s invocation of Articles 232 and 234 concerning KP raises two distinct constitutional questions: whether a grave security emergency exists and whether the provincial government can no longer function in accordance with the Constitution. Invoking both provisions together is not unconstitutional, but each requires an independent constitutional foundation.

Article 232 permits an emergency where internal disturbance threatens security beyond the provincial government’s power to control. Serious terrorism may support this threshold; however, political disagreement or dissatisfaction with provincial policy does not by itself establish it.

Article 234 addresses a different situation than the inability to carry on provincial government constitutionally.

As the President has invoked both Articles, the executive powers of the provincial government, i.e. the Chief Minister and Cabinet, will be exercised by the Federal Government or its nominated person. Furthermore, the legislative powers of the Provincial Assembly will also be exercised by Parliament.

Any judicial challenge must confront Article 236(2), which expressly bars questioning emergency proclamations and orders. Arguments concerning absent constitutional prerequisites or excess of authority require careful treatment of that bar.

More importantly, yes, all such actions involving the imposition of an emergency or Governor’s Rule are constitutional. However, we need to understand that the basic structure of our Constitution rests upon devolutionary federalism and democratic values, under which each province has its own elected representation and independent legislative and executive powers.
headline: KP emergency, governor's rule: Legal experts explain govt's constitutional powers

                                <div class="heading_H"><h1>Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as President Zardari approves summary on cabinet's advice</h1></div>
                                    <div class="except" style="margin-bottom: 12px;">
                        <h2>Centre cites shortcomings in KP govt's counterterrorism efforts amid worsening security situation in province</h2>
                    </div>
                                <div class="time-section"  >
                                            <div class="source">
                                                            <span class="by_author">By</span>



        <div class="author_title_img" style="color:#000">
                            <span class="author_agency">Web Desk</span>
            </div>
                                <span class="author_seperator"> | </span>

                              Published October 11, 2026                            </p>
                        </div>
                                        
                </div>

                <div class="story-area">
                    <div class="content-area">

<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.0 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/REC-html40/loose.dtd">
<html><body><div class="medium-insert-images ui-sortable"><figure contenteditable="false">
    <img src="https://www.geo.tv/assets/uploads/updates/2026-10-11/686054_4611785_updates.jpg" alt="President Asif Ali Zardari signs a bill in this undated picture. — President House/File" width="700" height="400" class="">

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">President Asif Ali Zardari signs a bill in this undated picture. — President House/File</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Federal cabinet cites security concerns and failed talks.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Governor Kundi to lead 11-member advisory council.</b></li><li><b><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Arrangement to remain in place for six months: law minister.</span><br></b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday proclaimed an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, citing the province's worsening security situation.</p><p>"The President approved and signed the summary upon the Prime Minister's advice under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan," the President Secretariat's Media Wing said in a press release.</p><style>

	<ins class="adsbygoogle"

	<script>
	     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
	</script>
	</div><p>The decision followed recommendations from the federal cabinet, formal advice from the prime minister and law-and-order reports submitted by relevant security institutions.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><iframe class="youtube-video" style="width:100%;height:350px;" src="//www.youtube.com/embed/NZqoLaoe_QU" allowfullscreen=""></iframe></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>The statement also cited the breakdown of negotiations between the government delegation and the provincial leadership over the deteriorating security situation.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2109193008969388380" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>The Centre had alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.</p><p>The Constitution allows the federal government to make provisions during an emergency, including suspending some constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies or authorities.</p><p>Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad that KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi would take charge with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council. He said the arrangement would initially remain in place for six months.</p><p>The development comes amid heightened political tensions following a long march led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.</p><p>The march began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed to reach an agreement.</p><p>The talks broke down over disagreements concerning counterterrorism cooperation in KP and access to incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, including a meeting with his personal doctor.</p><p>The government and opposition traded accusations over the failure to reach an agreement as Afridi continued leading the march through the province.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Governor backs emergency in KP</span></h2><p>Following the move, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that the province's people welcomed the presidential proclamation, adding that they wanted peace, stability, development and prosperity rather than unrest and insecurity.</p><p>In a video message addressed to KP residents, Kundi said the province's peace-loving people did not support terrorism or violent activities.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><iframe class="youtube-video" style="width:100%;height:350px;" src="//www.youtube.com/embed/NZqoLaoe_QU" allowfullscreen=""></iframe></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>He said they had resolved not to support Fitna al-Khawarij and would stand shoulder to shoulder with security forces in the fight against terrorists until their last breath.</p><p>The governor said residents wanted a peaceful and prosperous future, with brotherly relations and mutual cooperation with other provinces.</p><p>He urged them to maintain peace and refrain from violating the law, inciting violence or engaging in rioting, warning that action would be taken against those who disturbed law and order or took the law into their own hands.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Fazlur Rehman terms act 'attack on democracy' </span></h2><p>Separately, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has termed the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule an "attack on democracy", saying his party will reach out to the public and continue playing its role both inside and outside parliament.</p><p>Addressing a press conference, Fazlur Rehman said the government wanted the announcement of an end to the long march before accepting the protesters’ demands.</p><p>He said PTI had demanded permission to meet the party’s founder, Imran Khan.</p><p>The JUI-F chief said he had held discussions with Sohail Afridi, Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Shahram Khan Tarakai and Asad Qaiser regarding the situation.</p><p>According to Fazlur Rehman, PTI representatives had said they were ready to call off the long march if their demands were accepted.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Army deployed to assist administration</span></h2><p>The federal government has also approved the deployment of the Pakistan Army in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 245 of the Constitution, according to a notification.</p><p>The army will assist the administration, protect citizens’ lives and safeguard public property and government installations. The deployment will remain in place for the duration of the emergency imposed on October 11.</p><p>The KP governor will determine the number of troops in consultation with GHQ and the Military Operations Directorate, the notification said.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as President Zardari approves summary on cabinet's advice
subheadline: Centre cites shortcomings in KP govt's counterterrorism efforts amid worsening security situation in province
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Federal cabinet cites security concerns and failed talks.
Governor Kundi to lead 11-member advisory council.
Arrangement to remain in place for six months: law minister.

President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday proclaimed an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, citing the province's worsening security situation.

"The President approved and signed the summary upon the Prime Minister's advice under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan," the President Secretariat's Media Wing said in a press release.

The decision followed recommendations from the federal cabinet, formal advice from the prime minister and law-and-order reports submitted by relevant security institutions.

The statement also cited the breakdown of negotiations between the government delegation and the provincial leadership over the deteriorating security situation.

The Centre had alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.

The Constitution allows the federal government to make provisions during an emergency, including suspending some constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies or authorities.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad that KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi would take charge with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council. He said the arrangement would initially remain in place for six months.

The development comes amid heightened political tensions following a long march led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.

The march began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed to reach an agreement.

The talks broke down over disagreements concerning counterterrorism cooperation in KP and access to incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, including a meeting with his personal doctor.

The government and opposition traded accusations over the failure to reach an agreement as Afridi continued leading the march through the province.

Governor backs emergency in KP

Following the move, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that the province's people welcomed the presidential proclamation, adding that they wanted peace, stability, development and prosperity rather than unrest and insecurity.

In a video message addressed to KP residents, Kundi said the province's peace-loving people did not support terrorism or violent activities.

He said they had resolved not to support Fitna al-Khawarij and would stand shoulder to shoulder with security forces in the fight against terrorists until their last breath.

The governor said residents wanted a peaceful and prosperous future, with brotherly relations and mutual cooperation with other provinces.

He urged them to maintain peace and refrain from violating the law, inciting violence or engaging in rioting, warning that action would be taken against those who disturbed law and order or took the law into their own hands.

Fazlur Rehman terms act 'attack on democracy'

Separately, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has termed the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule an "attack on democracy", saying his party will reach out to the public and continue playing its role both inside and outside parliament.

Addressing a press conference, Fazlur Rehman said the government wanted the announcement of an end to the long march before accepting the protesters’ demands.

He said PTI had demanded permission to meet the party’s founder, Imran Khan.

The JUI-F chief said he had held discussions with Sohail Afridi, Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Shahram Khan Tarakai and Asad Qaiser regarding the situation.

According to Fazlur Rehman, PTI representatives had said they were ready to call off the long march if their demands were accepted.

Army deployed to assist administration

The federal government has also approved the deployment of the Pakistan Army in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 245 of the Constitution, according to a notification.

The army will assist the administration, protect citizens’ lives and safeguard public property and government installations. The deployment will remain in place for the duration of the emergency imposed on October 11.

The KP governor will determine the number of troops in consultation with GHQ and the Military Operations Directorate, the notification said.

• Federal cabinet cites security concerns and failed talks.
  • Governor Kundi to lead 11-member advisory council.
  • Arrangement to remain in place for six months: law minister.

President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday proclaimed an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, citing the province's worsening security situation.

"The President approved and signed the summary upon the Prime Minister's advice under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan," the President Secretariat's Media Wing said in a press release.

The decision followed recommendations from the federal cabinet, formal advice from the prime minister and law-and-order reports submitted by relevant security institutions.

The statement also cited the breakdown of negotiations between the government delegation and the provincial leadership over the deteriorating security situation.

The Centre had alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.

The Constitution allows the federal government to make provisions during an emergency, including suspending some constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies or authorities.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad that KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi would take charge with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council. He said the arrangement would initially remain in place for six months.

The development comes amid heightened political tensions following a long march led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.

The march began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed to reach an agreement.

The talks broke down over disagreements concerning counterterrorism cooperation in KP and access to incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, including a meeting with his personal doctor.

The government and opposition traded accusations over the failure to reach an agreement as Afridi continued leading the march through the province.

Governor backs emergency in KP

Following the move, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that the province's people welcomed the presidential proclamation, adding that they wanted peace, stability, development and prosperity rather than unrest and insecurity.

In a video message addressed to KP residents, Kundi said the province's peace-loving people did not support terrorism or violent activities.

He said they had resolved not to support Fitna al-Khawarij and would stand shoulder to shoulder with security forces in the fight against terrorists until their last breath.

The governor said residents wanted a peaceful and prosperous future, with brotherly relations and mutual cooperation with other provinces.

He urged them to maintain peace and refrain from violating the law, inciting violence or engaging in rioting, warning that action would be taken against those who disturbed law and order or took the law into their own hands.

Fazlur Rehman terms act 'attack on democracy'

Separately, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has termed the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule an "attack on democracy", saying his party will reach out to the public and continue playing its role both inside and outside parliament.

Addressing a press conference, Fazlur Rehman said the government wanted the announcement of an end to the long march before accepting the protesters’ demands.

He said PTI had demanded permission to meet the party’s founder, Imran Khan.

The JUI-F chief said he had held discussions with Sohail Afridi, Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Shahram Khan Tarakai and Asad Qaiser regarding the situation.

According to Fazlur Rehman, PTI representatives had said they were ready to call off the long march if their demands were accepted.

Army deployed to assist administration

The federal government has also approved the deployment of the Pakistan Army in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 245 of the Constitution, according to a notification.

The army will assist the administration, protect citizens’ lives and safeguard public property and government installations. The deployment will remain in place for the duration of the emergency imposed on October 11.

The KP governor will determine the number of troops in consultation with GHQ and the Military Operations Directorate, the notification said.

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="" spellcheck="false">(From left) Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi during a press conference in Islamabad, on October 11, 2026. — Geo News</figcaption><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><superhuman-go-underlines data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; display: contents; --rem: 16;"></superhuman-go-underlines></figure></div><ul><li><b>Law Minister Tarar says terror incidents in province rose 196%.</b></li><li><b>Ministers cite worsening security behind emergency decision.</b></li><li><b>Naqvi says PTI negotiations continued until midnight.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday defended the imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying the government faced a choice between witnessing daily martyrdoms or taking a “difficult decision”.</p><p>“We had two options: either we witness martyrdoms on a daily basis or take a difficult decision,” Naqvi told a press conference in Islamabad alongside Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.</p><style>

	</div><p>Naqvi said the decision had been taken against the backdrop of the security situation in the province, maintaining that the federal government had tried for more than a month to bring the KP government on board in the fight against terrorism.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><iframe class="youtube-video" style="width:100%;height:350px;" src="//www.youtube.com/embed/_ktKgH_N3e4" allowfullscreen=""></iframe></div>
		</div>

	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>“Today was not an easy day for us,” the interior minister said, adding that he had personally remained in contact with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government behind the scenes.</p><p>“Our objective was to bring them on board so that we could fight the war against terrorism together,” he added.</p><p>Naqvi said the federal government had no issue with the PTI’s sit-in, maintaining that it could deal with the protest.</p><p>“Our issue is terrorism,” he said.</p><p>The interior minister said the government remained in contact with PTI leaders until around 11:45pm and sought their response on proposed changes to a draft.</p><p>“I called them at around 11:45pm and asked them to respond so that this situation could be avoided,” he said.</p><p>Naqvi said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also met Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman as part of the efforts, but no response was received.</p><p>He said the government had earlier held two days of negotiations with the PTI, during which Asad Qaiser had made it clear that his party would cooperate in the fight against terrorism.</p><p>According to Naqvi, the draft under discussion was changed three times and revised for a fourth time at the PTI’s request.</p><p>“When the fourth draft was finalised, they backed out,” he claimed.</p><p>Naqvi said he had also held several meetings with Sohail Afridi, maintaining that terrorism was the only subject discussed during those interactions and that no political matters were taken up.</p><p>He said it had been agreed four months ago to enhance police capacity in five districts, with the federal government offering to address a shortage of funds raised by Afridi.</p><p>The interior minister claimed that during the first round of negotiations, the provincial side had agreed to the imposition of emergency in 12 districts.</p><p>Naqvi said the security situation in those districts was “very bad”, questioning how the PTI had nevertheless taken its long march through the affected areas.</p><p>The interior minister maintained that the government’s position was clear that terrorism had nothing to do with politics.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Terror incidents increased 196%: Tarar</span></h2><p>Speaking on the occasion, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said terrorism incidents in KP had increased by 196%, describing the figure as the “most alarming” aspect of the situation.</p><p>He said terrorism had become a routine occurrence in the province and accused the provincial government of pursuing its politics while neglecting the protection of the public.</p><p>Tarar said the federal cabinet decided to impose the emergency after considering the circumstances in the province, adding that the KP governor had also conveyed “very concerning” developments to the federal government.</p><p>“Such steps are not taken happily,” the law minister said, maintaining that emergency powers should be exercised in the interest of national security and the country.</p><p>Tarar said the president had acted within the Constitution by exercising powers provided under Articles 232 and 234.</p><p>He said the provincial government had ceased to function under the emergency, with the governor empowered to administer the province under the federation.</p><p>The law minister added that the governor would be assisted by an 11-member advisory council, while a separate secretariat had been established for 12 districts severely affected by terrorism.</p><p>Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, meanwhile, accused the former provincial government of having a “nexus” with terrorists and alleged that it had effectively “outsourced” some districts to them.</p><p>He claimed there was “irrefutable evidence” that the provincial government was pushing KP towards destruction.</p><p>The information minister said the advisory council would comprise technocrats, including Lt Gen (retd) Nigar Johar, Kifayatullah Khan, Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Aamir Javed, Dr Aamir Abdullah, Dr Sarfaraz Ali Shah, Dr Muhammad Irshad, Asif Rafiq Afridi, Tayyab Qureshi, Usman Saifullah Khan and Samar Haroon Bilour.</p>                    </div>

headline: Ministers defend KP emergency as choice between 'daily martyrdoms', tough decision
subheadline: Info Minister Attaullah Tarar accuses PTI KP govt of having a "nexus" with terrorists
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Law Minister Tarar says terror incidents in province rose 196%.
Ministers cite worsening security behind emergency decision.
Naqvi says PTI negotiations continued until midnight.

ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday defended the imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying the government faced a choice between witnessing daily martyrdoms or taking a “difficult decision”.

“We had two options: either we witness martyrdoms on a daily basis or take a difficult decision,” Naqvi told a press conference in Islamabad alongside Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Naqvi said the decision had been taken against the backdrop of the security situation in the province, maintaining that the federal government had tried for more than a month to bring the KP government on board in the fight against terrorism.

“Today was not an easy day for us,” the interior minister said, adding that he had personally remained in contact with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government behind the scenes.

“Our objective was to bring them on board so that we could fight the war against terrorism together,” he added.

Naqvi said the federal government had no issue with the PTI’s sit-in, maintaining that it could deal with the protest.

“Our issue is terrorism,” he said.

The interior minister said the government remained in contact with PTI leaders until around 11:45pm and sought their response on proposed changes to a draft.

“I called them at around 11:45pm and asked them to respond so that this situation could be avoided,” he said.

Naqvi said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also met Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman as part of the efforts, but no response was received.

He said the government had earlier held two days of negotiations with the PTI, during which Asad Qaiser had made it clear that his party would cooperate in the fight against terrorism.

According to Naqvi, the draft under discussion was changed three times and revised for a fourth time at the PTI’s request.

“When the fourth draft was finalised, they backed out,” he claimed.

Naqvi said he had also held several meetings with Sohail Afridi, maintaining that terrorism was the only subject discussed during those interactions and that no political matters were taken up.

He said it had been agreed four months ago to enhance police capacity in five districts, with the federal government offering to address a shortage of funds raised by Afridi.

The interior minister claimed that during the first round of negotiations, the provincial side had agreed to the imposition of emergency in 12 districts.

Naqvi said the security situation in those districts was “very bad”, questioning how the PTI had nevertheless taken its long march through the affected areas.

The interior minister maintained that the government’s position was clear that terrorism had nothing to do with politics.

Terror incidents increased 196%: Tarar

Speaking on the occasion, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said terrorism incidents in KP had increased by 196%, describing the figure as the “most alarming” aspect of the situation.

He said terrorism had become a routine occurrence in the province and accused the provincial government of pursuing its politics while neglecting the protection of the public.

Tarar said the federal cabinet decided to impose the emergency after considering the circumstances in the province, adding that the KP governor had also conveyed “very concerning” developments to the federal government.

“Such steps are not taken happily,” the law minister said, maintaining that emergency powers should be exercised in the interest of national security and the country.

Tarar said the president had acted within the Constitution by exercising powers provided under Articles 232 and 234.

He said the provincial government had ceased to function under the emergency, with the governor empowered to administer the province under the federation.

The law minister added that the governor would be assisted by an 11-member advisory council, while a separate secretariat had been established for 12 districts severely affected by terrorism.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, meanwhile, accused the former provincial government of having a “nexus” with terrorists and alleged that it had effectively “outsourced” some districts to them.

He claimed there was “irrefutable evidence” that the provincial government was pushing KP towards destruction.

The information minister said the advisory council would comprise technocrats, including Lt Gen (retd) Nigar Johar, Kifayatullah Khan, Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Aamir Javed, Dr Aamir Abdullah, Dr Sarfaraz Ali Shah, Dr Muhammad Irshad, Asif Rafiq Afridi, Tayyab Qureshi, Usman Saifullah Khan and Samar Haroon Bilour.

Law Minister Tarar says terror incidents in province rose 196%.

Ministers cite worsening security behind emergency decision.

Naqvi says PTI negotiations continued until midnight.

ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday defended the imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying the government faced a choice between witnessing daily martyrdoms or taking a “difficult decision”.

“We had two options: either we witness martyrdoms on a daily basis or take a difficult decision,” Naqvi told a press conference in Islamabad alongside Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Naqvi said the decision had been taken against the backdrop of the security situation in the province, maintaining that the federal government had tried for more than a month to bring the KP government on board in the fight against terrorism.

“Today was not an easy day for us,” the interior minister said, adding that he had personally remained in contact with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government behind the scenes.

“Our objective was to bring them on board so that we could fight the war against terrorism together,” he added.

Naqvi said the federal government had no issue with the PTI’s sit-in, maintaining that it could deal with the protest.

“Our issue is terrorism,” he said.

The interior minister said the government remained in contact with PTI leaders until around 11:45pm and sought their response on proposed changes to a draft.

“I called them at around 11:45pm and asked them to respond so that this situation could be avoided,” he said.

Naqvi said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also met Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman as part of the efforts, but no response was received.

He said the government had earlier held two days of negotiations with the PTI, during which Asad Qaiser had made it clear that his party would cooperate in the fight against terrorism.

According to Naqvi, the draft under discussion was changed three times and revised for a fourth time at the PTI’s request.

“When the fourth draft was finalised, they backed out,” he claimed.

Naqvi said he had also held several meetings with Sohail Afridi, maintaining that terrorism was the only subject discussed during those interactions and that no political matters were taken up.

He said it had been agreed four months ago to enhance police capacity in five districts, with the federal government offering to address a shortage of funds raised by Afridi.

The interior minister claimed that during the first round of negotiations, the provincial side had agreed to the imposition of emergency in 12 districts.

Naqvi said the security situation in those districts was “very bad”, questioning how the PTI had nevertheless taken its long march through the affected areas.

The interior minister maintained that the government’s position was clear that terrorism had nothing to do with politics.

Terror incidents increased 196%: Tarar

Speaking on the occasion, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said terrorism incidents in KP had increased by 196%, describing the figure as the “most alarming” aspect of the situation.

He said terrorism had become a routine occurrence in the province and accused the provincial government of pursuing its politics while neglecting the protection of the public.

Tarar said the federal cabinet decided to impose the emergency after considering the circumstances in the province, adding that the KP governor had also conveyed “very concerning” developments to the federal government.

“Such steps are not taken happily,” the law minister said, maintaining that emergency powers should be exercised in the interest of national security and the country.

Tarar said the president had acted within the Constitution by exercising powers provided under Articles 232 and 234.

He said the provincial government had ceased to function under the emergency, with the governor empowered to administer the province under the federation.

The law minister added that the governor would be assisted by an 11-member advisory council, while a separate secretariat had been established for 12 districts severely affected by terrorism.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, meanwhile, accused the former provincial government of having a “nexus” with terrorists and alleged that it had effectively “outsourced” some districts to them.

He claimed there was “irrefutable evidence” that the provincial government was pushing KP towards destruction.

The information minister said the advisory council would comprise technocrats, including Lt Gen (retd) Nigar Johar, Kifayatullah Khan, Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Aamir Javed, Dr Aamir Abdullah, Dr Sarfaraz Ali Shah, Dr Muhammad Irshad, Asif Rafiq Afridi, Tayyab Qureshi, Usman Saifullah Khan and Samar Haroon Bilour.
